text: And they have said that they want to see Israel wiped off the map.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So the work that we've done with respect to sanctions now offers Iran a choice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They can take the diplomatic route and end their nuclear program or they will have to face a united world and a United States president, me, who said we're not going to take any options off the table.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The disagreement I have with Governor Romney is that, during the course of this campaign, he's often talked as if we should take premature military action.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I think that would be a mistake, because when I've sent young men and women into harm's way, I always understand that that is the last resort, not the first resort.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Well, first of all, I want to underscore the same point the president mad,e which is that if I'm President of the United States, when I'm President of the United States, we will stand with Israel.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And if Israel is attacked, we have their back, not just diplomatically, not just culturally, but militarily.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Number two, with regards to Iran and the threat of Iran, there's no question but that a nuclear Iran, a nuclear-capable Iran is unacceptable to America.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It presents a threat not only to our friends but ultimately a threat to us to have Iran have nuclear material, nuclear weapons that could be used against us or used to be threatening to us.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It is also essential for us to understand what our mission is in Iran, and that is to dissuade Iran from having a nuclear weapon through peaceful and diplomatic means.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And crippling sanctions are something I called for five years ago, when I was in Israel, speaking at the Herzliya Conference.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I laid out seven steps, crippling sanctions were number one.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: You're seeing it right now in the economy.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It's absolutely the right thing to do, to have crippling sanctions.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I would have put them in place earlier.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But it's good that we have them.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Number two, something I would add today is I would tighten those sanctions.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I would say that ships that carry Iranian oil, can't come into our ports.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: would agree with us as well.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Not only ships couldn't, but I'd say companies that are moving their oil can't, people who are trading in their oil can't.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I would tighten those sanctions further.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Secondly, I'd take on diplomatic isolation efforts.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'd make sure that Ahmadinejad is indicted under the Genocide Convention.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: His words amount to genocide incitation.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I would indict him for it.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I would also make sure that their diplomats are treated like the pariah they are around the world.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: The same way we treated the apartheid diplomats of South Africa.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We need to increase pressure time, and time again on Iran because anything other than a -- a -- a solution to this, which says -- which stops this -- this nuclear folly of theirs, is unacceptable to America.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And of course, a military action is the last resort.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It is something one would only - only consider if all of the other avenues had been -- had been tried to their full extent.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, first of all those are reports in the newspaper.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But our goal is to get Iran to recognize it needs to give up its nuclear program and abide by the U.N. resolutions that have been in place.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because they have the opportunity to reenter the community of nations, and we would welcome that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There -- there are people in Iran who have the same aspirations as people all around the world for a better life.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we hope that their leadership takes the right decision, but the deal we'll accept is they end their nuclear program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I'm glad that Governor Romney agrees with the steps that we're taking.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You know, there have been times, Governor, frankly, during the course of this campaign, where it sounded like you thought that you'd do the same things we did, but you'd say them louder and somehow that -- that would make a difference.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it turns out that the work involved in setting up these crippling sanctions is painstaking.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We started from the day we got into office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the reason is was so important -- and this is a testament to how we've restored American credibility and strength around the world -- is we had to make sure that all the countries participated, even countries like Russia and China.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because if it's just us that are imposing sanctions -- we've had sanctions in place a long time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's because we got everybody to agree that Iran is seeing so much pressure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we've got to maintain that pressure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There is a deal to be had, and that is that they abide by the rules that have already been established.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They convince the international community they are not pursuing a nuclear program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are inspections that are very intrusive.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But over time, what they can do is regain credibility.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the meantime, though, we're not going to let up the pressure until we have clear evidence that that takes place.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And one last thing -- just -- just to make this point.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're not going to allow Iran to perpetually engage in negotiations that lead nowhere.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I've been very clear to them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You know, because of the intelligence coordination that we do with a range of countries, including Israel, we have a sense of when they would get breakout capacity, which means that we would not be able to intervene in time to stop their nuclear program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that clock is ticking.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I think from the very beginning, one of the challenges we've had with Iran is that they have looked at this administration, and felt that the administration was not as strong as it needed to be.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I think they saw weakness where they had expected to find American strength.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And I say that because from the very beginning, the president in his campaign four years ago, said he would meet with all the world's worst actors in his first year, he'd sit down with Chavez and Kim Jong-il, with Castro and President Ahmadinejad of Iran.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And I think they looked and thought, well, that's an unusual honor to receive from the President of the United States.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And then the president began what I have called an apology tour, of going to various nations in the Middle East and criticizing America.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I think they looked at that and saw weakness.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Then when there were dissidents in the streets of Tehran, a Green Revolution, holding signs saying, is America with us, the president was silent.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I think they noticed that as well.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And I think that when the president said he was going to create daylight between ourselves and Israel, that they noticed that as well.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: All of these things suggested, I think, to the Iranian mullahs that, hey, you know, we can keep on pushing along here, we can keep talks going on, we're just going to keep on spinning centrifuges.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Now there are some 10,000 centrifuges spinning uranium, preparing to create a nuclear threat to the United States and to the world.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: That's unacceptable for us, and it's essential for a president to show strength from the very beginning, to make it very clear what is acceptable and not acceptable.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And an Iranian nuclear program is not acceptable to us.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They must not develop nuclear capability.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They need to be tightened.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Our diplomatic isolation needs to be tougher.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We need to indict Ahmadinejad.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We need to put the pressure on them as hard as we possibly can, because if we do that, we won't have to take the military action.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Bob, let me just respond.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Nothing Governor Romney just said is true, starting with this notion of me apologizing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This has been probably the biggest whopper that's been told during the course of this campaign.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And every fact checker and every reporter who's looked at it, Governor, has said this is not true.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when it comes to tightening sanctions, look, as I said before, we've put in the toughest, most crippling sanctions ever.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the fact is, while we were coordinating an international coalition to make sure these sanctions were effective, you were still invested in a Chinese state oil company that was doing business with the Iranian oil sector.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I'll let the American people decide, judge, who's going to be more effective and more credible when it comes to imposing crippling sanctions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And with respect to our attitude about the Iranian revolution, I was very clear about the murderous activities that had taken place and that was contrary to international law and everything that civilized people stand for.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And -- and so the strength that we have shown in Iran is shown by the fact that we've been able to mobilize the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When I came into office, the world was divided.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Iran is at its weakest point, economically, strategically, militarily, then since -- then in many years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we are going to continue to keep the pressure on to make sure that they do not get a nuclear weapon.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's in America's national interest and that will be the case so long as I'm president.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We're four years closer to a nuclear Iran.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And -- and -- we should not have wasted these four years to the extent they -- they continue to be able to spin these centrifuges and get that much closer.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Number two, Mr. President, the reason I call it an apology tour is because you went to the Middle East and you flew to Egypt and to Saudi Arabia and to Turkey and Iraq.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And by the way, you skipped Israel, our closest friend in the region, but you went to the other nations.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And by the way, they noticed that you skipped Israel.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And then in those nations, and on Arabic TV, you said that America had been dismissive and derisive.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: You said that on occasion America had dictated to other nations.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Mr. President, America has not dictated to other nations.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We have freed other nations from dictators.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Bob, let me -- let me respond.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we're going to talk about trips that we've taken -- when I was a candidate for office, first trip I took was to visit our troops.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when I went to Israel as a candidate, I didn't take donors.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I went to Yad Beshef (ph), the Holocaust museum there, to remind myself the nature of evil and why our bond with Israel will be unbreakable.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And then I went down to the border towns of Storok (ph), which had experienced missiles raining dowm from Hamas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I saw families there who showed me there where missiles had come down near their children's bedrooms.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I was reminded of what that would mean if those were my kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Which is why as president, we funded an Iron Dome program to stop those missiles.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So that's how I've used my travels, when I travel to Israel and when I travel to the region.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the -- the central question at this point is going to be: Who is going to be credible to all parties involved?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And they can look at my track record, whether it's Iran sanctions, whether it's dealing with counterterrorism, whether it's supporting democracy, whether it's supporting women's rights, whether it's supporting religious minorities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And they can say that the President of the United States and the United States of America has stood on the right side of history.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that kind of credibility is precisely why we've been able to show leadership on a wide range of issues facing the world right now.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Bob, let's not go into hypotheticals of that nature.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Our relationship with Israel, my relationship with the prime minister of Israel is such that we would not get a call saying our bombers are on the way, or their fighters are on the way.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: This is the kind of thing that would have been discussed and thoroughly evaluated well before that kind of --

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But let me -- let me come back -- we can come back.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Let's come back to what the president was speaking about, which is what's happening in the world and the president's statement that things are going so well.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Look, I look at what's happening around the world, and i see Iran four years closer to a bomb.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I see the Middle East with a rising tide of violence, chaos, tumult.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I see jihadists continuing to spread, whether they're rising or just about the same level, hard to precisely measure, but it's clear they're there.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I see Syria with 30,000 civilians dead, Assad still in power.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I see our trade deficit with China, larger than it's -- growing larger every year, as a matter of fact.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I look around the world and I don't feel that you see North Korea, continuing to export their nuclear technology, Russia said they're not going to follow Nunn-Lugar any more.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They're back away from a nuclear proliferation treaty that we had with them.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I look around the world, I don't see our influence growing around the world.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I see our influence receding, in part because of the failure of the president to deal with our economic challenges at home; in part because of our withdrawal from our commitment to our military in the way I think it ought to be; in part because of the -- the -- the turmoil with Israel.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I mean, the president received a letter from 38 Democrat senators saying the tensions with Israel were a real problem.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They asked him, please repair the tension -- Democrat senators -- please repair the tension...

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: ... the damage in his -- in his own party.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Governor, the problem is, is that on a whole range of issues, whether it's the Middle East, whether it's Afghanistan, whether it's Iraq, whether it's now Iran, you've been all over the map.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I mean, I'm -- I'm pleased that you now are endorsing our policy of applying diplomatic pressure and potentially having bilateral discussions with the Iranians to end their nuclear program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But just a few years ago you said that's something you'd never do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the same way that you initially opposed a timetable in Afghanistan, now you're for it, although it depends.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the same way that you say you would have ended the war in Iraq, but recently gave a speech saying that we should have 20,000 more folks in there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The same way that you said that it was mission creep to go after Gadhafi.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When it comes to going after Osama bin Laden, you said, well, any president would make that call.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But when you were a candidate in 2008, as I was, and I said if I got bin Laden in our sights I would take that shot, you said we shouldn't move heaven and earth to get one man.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And you said we should ask Pakistan for permission.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if we had asked Pakistan permission, we would not have gotten him.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it was worth moving heaven and earth to get him.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You know, after we killed bin Laden I was at ground zero for a memorial and talked to a young women who was four years old when 9/11 happened.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the last conversation she had with her father was him calling from the twin towers, saying "Peyton (ph), I love you and I will always watch over you."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And for the next decade, she was haunted by that conversation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And she said to me, "You know, by finally getting bin Laden, that brought some closure to me."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when we do things like that -- when we bring those who have harmed us to justice, that sends a message to the world and it tells Peyton (ph) that we did not forget her father.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I make that point because that's the kind of clarity of leadership, and those decisions are not always popular.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those decisions generally -- generally are not poll-tested.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And even some in my own party, including my current vice president, had the same critique as you did.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But what the American people understand is that I look at what we need to get done to keep the American people safe and to move our interests forward, and I make those decisions.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: You can't -- but you can't have the president just lay out a whole series of items without giving me a chance to respond.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Well, we're going to be finished by 2014, and when I'm president, we'll make sure we bring our troops out by the end of 2014.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: The commanders and the generals there are on track to do so.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We've seen progress over the past several years.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: The surge has been successful and the training program is proceeding apace.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: There are now a large number of Afghan Security Forces, 350,000 that are ready to step in to provide security and we're going to be able to make that transition by the end of 2014.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: So our troops will come home at that point.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I can tell you at the same time, that we will make sure that we look at what's happening in Pakistan, and recognize that what's happening in Pakistan is going to have a major impact on the success in Afghanistan.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And I say that because I know a lot of people that feel like we should just brush our hands and walk away.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And I don't mean you, Mr. President, but some people in the -- in our nation feel that Pakistan is being nice to us, and that we should walk away fro mthem.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But Pakistan is important to the region, to the world and to us, because Pakistan has 100 nuclear warheads and they're rushing to build a lot more.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They'll have more than Great Britain sometime in the -- in the relatively near future.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They also have the Haqqani Network and the Taliban existent within their country.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And so a Pakistan that falls apart, becomes a failed state, would be of extraordinary danger to Afghanistan and to us.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And so we're going to have to remain helpful in encouraging Pakistan to move towards a more stable government and rebuild the relationship with us.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And that means that our aid that we provide to Pakistan is going to have to be conditioned upon certain benchmarks being met.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: So for me, I look at this as both a need to help move Pakistan in the right direction, and also to get Afghanistan to be ready, and they will be ready by the end of 2014.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When I came into office, we were still bogged down in Iraq and Afghanistan had been drifting for a decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We ended the war in Iraq, refocused our attention on Afghanistan, and we did deliver a surge of troops.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That was facilitated in part because we had ended the war in Iraq.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we are now in a position where we have met many of the objectives that got us there in the first place.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Part of what had happened is we'd forgotten why we had gone.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We went because there were people who were responsible for 3,000 American deaths.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And so we decimated Al Qaida's core leadership in the border regions between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We then started to build up Afghan forces.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we're now in a position where we can transition out, because there's no reason why Americans should die when Afghans are perfectly capable of defending their own country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, that transition has to take place in a responsible fashion.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've been there a long time, and we've got to make sure that we and our coalition partners are pulling out responsibly and giving Afghans the capabilities that they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But what I think the American people recognize is after a decade of war it's time to do some nation building here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And what we can now do is free up some resources, to, for example, put Americans back to work, especially our veterans, rebuilding our roads, our bridges, our schools, making sure that, you know, our veterans are getting the care that they need when it comes to post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injury, making sure that the certifications that they need for good jobs of the future are in place.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You know, I was having lunch with some -- a veteran in Minnesota who had been a medic dealing with the most extreme circumstances.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When he came home and he wanted to become a nurse, he had to start from scratch.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And what we've said is let's change those certifications.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The first lady has done great work with an organization called Joining Forces putting our veterans back to work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as a consequence, veterans' unemployment is actually now lower than general population.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It was higher when I came into office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So those are the kinds of things that we can now do because we're making that transition in Afghanistan.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: No, it's not time to divorce a nation on Earth that has 100 nuclear weapons and is on the way to double that at some point, a nation that has serious threats from terrorist groups within its nation, as I indicated before, the Taliban, Haqqani Network.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It's a nation that's not like -- like others and it does not have a civilian leadership that is calling the shots there.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: You have the ISI, their intelligence organization, is probably the most powerful of the -- of three branches there.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Then you have the military and then you have the civilian government.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: This is a nation, which, if it falls apart, if it -- if it becomes a failed state, there are nuclear weapons there and you've got -- you've got terrorists there who could grab their -- their hands onto those nuclear weapons.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: This is -- this is an important part of the world for us.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Pakistan is -- is technically an ally, and they're not acting very much like an ally right now.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But we have some work to do.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And I -- I don't blame the administration for the fact that the relationship with Pakistan is strained.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We -- we had to go into Pakistan.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We had to go in there to get Osama bin Laden.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: That was the right thing to do.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And -- and that upset them, but obviously there was a great deal of anger even before that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But we're going to have to work with the -- with the people in Pakistan to try and help them move to a more responsible course than the one that they're on.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And it's important for them.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It's important for the nuclear weapons.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It's important for the success of Afghanistan.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Because inside Pakistan, you have a -- a large group of Pashtun that are -- that are Taliban.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And that's one of the reasons the Afghan Security Forces have so much work to do to be able to fight against that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But it's important for us to recognize that we can't just walk away from Pakistan.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But we do need to make sure that as we -- as we send support for them, that this is tied to them making progress on -- on matters that would lead them to becoming a civil society.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And it's widely reported that drones are being used in drone strikes, and I support that and entirely, and feel the president was right to up the usage of that technology, and believe that we should continue to use it, to continue to go after the people that represent a threat to this nation and to our friends.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But let me also note that as I said earlier, we're going to have to do more than just going after leaders and -- and killing bad guys, important as that is.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We're also going to have to have a farm more effective and comprehensive strategy to help move the world away from terror and Islamic extremism.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We haven't done that yet.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We talk a lot about these things, but you look at the -- the record, you look at the record.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: You look at the record of the last four years and say is Iran closer to a bomb?

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Is the Middle East in tumult?

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Is -- is al-Qaida on the run, on its heels?

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Is -- are Israel and the Palestinians closer to reaching a peace agreement?

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: No, they haven't had talks in two years.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We have not seen the progress we need to have, and I'm convinced that with strong leadership and an effort to build a strategy based upon helping these nations reject extremism, we can see the kind of peace and prosperity the world demands.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, keep in mind our strategy wasn't just going after bin Laden.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We created partnerships throughout the region to deal with extremism in Somalia, in Yemen, in Pakistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And what we've also done is engaged these governments in the kind of reforms that are actually going to make a difference in people's lives day to day, to make sure that their governments aren't corrupt, to make sure that they're treating women with the kind of respect and dignity that every nation that succeeds has shown and to make sure that they've got a free market system that works.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So across the board, we are engaging them in building capacity in these countries.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we have stood on the side of democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One thing I think Americans should be proud of, when Tunisians began to protest, this nation -- me, my administration -- stood with them earlier than just about any country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Egypt we stood on the side of democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Libya we stood on the side of the people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as a consequence, there's no doubt that attitudes about Americans have changed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But there are always going to be elements in these countries that potentially threaten the United States.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we want to shrink those groups and those networks and we can do that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we're always also going to have to maintain vigilance when it comes to terrorist activities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The truth, though, is that Al Qaeda is much weaker than it was when I came into office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And they don't have the same capacities to attack the U.S. homeland and our allies as they did four years ago.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, I think it will continue to be terrorist networks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But with respect to China, China is both an adversary, but also a potential partner in the international community if it's following the rules.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So my attitude coming into office was that we are going to insist that China plays by the same rules as everybody else.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know Americans had seen jobs being shipped overseas; businesses and workers not getting a level playing field when it came to trade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's the reason why I set up a trade task force to go after cheaters when it came to international trade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the reason why we have brought more cases against China for violating trade rules than the other -- the previous administration had done in two terms.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we've won just about every case that we've filed, that has been decided.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, just recently steelworkers in Ohio and throughout the Midwest -- Pennsylvania -- are in a position now to sell steel to China because we won that case.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We had a tire case in which they were flooding us with cheap domestic tires -- or -- or cheap Chinese tires.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we put a stop to it and as a consequence saved jobs throughout America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I have to say that Governor Romney criticized me for being too tough in that tire case; said this wouldn't be good for American workers and that it would be protectionist.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I tell you, those workers don't feel that way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They feel as if they had finally an administration who was going to take this issue seriously.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the long term, in order for us to compete with China, we've also got to make sure, though, that we're taking -- taking care of business here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we don't have the best education system in the world, if we don't continue to put money into research and technology that will allow us to create great businesses here in the United States, that's how we lose the competition.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And, unfortunately, Governor Romney's budget and his proposals would not allow us to make those investments.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Well, first of all, it's not government that makes business successful.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It's not government investments that makes businesses grow and hire people.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Let me also note that the greatest threat that the world faces, the greatest national security threat is a nuclear Iran.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: China has an interest that's very much like ours in one respect, and that is they want a stable world.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They don't want to see protectionism.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They don't want to see the world break out into -- into various forms of chaos, because they have to -- they have to manufacture goods and put people to work and they have about 20,000 -- 20 million, rather, people coming out of the farms every year coming into the cities, needing jobs.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: So they want the economy to work and the world to be free and open.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And so we can be a partner with China.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We don't have to be an adversary in any way, shape or form.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We can work with them, we can collaborate with them, if they're willing to be responsible.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Now, they look at us and say, Is it a good idea to be with America?

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: How strong are we going to be?

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: How strong is our economy?

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They look at the fact that we owe 'em a trillion dollars and owe other people $16 trillion in total, including that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They look at our -- our decision to -- to cut back on our military capabilities.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: The secretary of defense called these trillion dollars of cuts to our military devastating.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It's not my term, it's the president's own secretary of defense called these trillion dollars of cuts to our military devastating.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It's not my term, it's the president's own Secretary of Defense, called them devastating.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They look at America's commitments around the world and they see what's happening, and they say, well, OK. Is America going to be strong?

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And the answer is, yes, if I'm president, America will be very strong.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We'll also make sure that we have trade relations with China that work for us.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I've watched year in and year out as companies have shut down and people have lost their jobs because China has not played by the same rules, in part by holding down artificially the value of their currency.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It holds down the prices of their goods.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It means our goods aren't as competitive and we lose jobs.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They're making some progress; they need to make more.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: That's why on day one, i will label them a currency manipulator, which allows us to apply tariffs where they're taking jobs.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They're stealing our intellectual property, our patents, our designs, our technology, hacking into our computers, counterfeiting our goods.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They have to understand we want to trade with them.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We want a world that's stable.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We like free enterprise, but you got to play by the rules.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Well, they sell us about this much stuff every year, and we sell them about this much stuff every year.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: So it's pretty clear who doesn't want a trade war.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And there's one going on right now, which we don't know about it.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We have enormous trade imbalance with China, and it's worse this year than last year, and it's worse last year than the year before.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And so we have to understand that we can't just surrender and lose jobs year in and year out.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We have to say to our friend in China, look, you guys are playing aggressively.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But this can't keep on going.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: You can't keep on holding down the value of your currency, stealing our intellectual property, counterfeiting our products, selling them around the world, even to the United States.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I was with one company that makes valves and -- and process industries and they said, look, we were -- we were having some valves coming in that -- that were broken and we had to repair them under warranty and we looked them and -- and they had our serial number on them.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And then we noticed that there was more than one with that same serial number.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They were counterfeit products being made overseas with the same serial number as a U.S. company, the same packaging, these were being sold into our market and around the world as if they were made by the U.S. competitor.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I want a great relationship with China.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: China can be our partner, but -- but that doesn't mean they can just roll all over us and steal our jobs on an unfair basis.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, Governor Romney's right, you are familiar with jobs being shipped overseas because you invested in companies that were shipping jobs overseas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And, you know, that's -- you're right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I mean that's how our free market works.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I've made a different bet on American workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we had taken your advice Governor Romney about our auto industry, we'd be buying cars from China instead of selling cars to China.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we take your advice with respect to how we change our tax codes so that companies that earn profits overseas don't pay U.S. taxes compared to companies here that are paying taxes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now that's estimated to create 800,000 jobs, the problem is they won't be here, they'll be in places like China.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if we're not making investments in education and basic research, which is not something that the private sector is doing at a sufficient pace right now and has never done, then we will lose the (inaudible) in things like clean energy technology.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now with respect to what we've done with China already, U.S. exports have doubled since I came into office, to China and actually currencies are at their most advantageous point for U.S. exporters since 1993.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We absolutely have to make more progress and that's why we're going to keep on pressing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when it comes to our military and Chinese security, part of the reason that we were able to pivot to the Asia-Pacific region after having ended the war in Iraq and transitioning out of Afghanistan, is precisely because this is going to be a massive growth area in the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we believe China can be a partner, but we're also sending a very clear signal that America is a Pacific power; that we are going to have a presence there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are working with countries in the region to make sure, for example, that ships can pass through; that commerce continues.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we're organizing trade relations with countries other than China so that China starts feeling more pressure about meeting basic international standards.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the kind of leadership we've shown in the region.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the kind of leadership that we'll continue to show.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I just want to take one of those points, again, attacking me as not talking about an agenda for -- for getting more trade and opening up more jobs in this country.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But the president mentioned the auto industry and that somehow I would be in favor of jobs being elsewhere.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Nothing could be further from the truth.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'm a son of Detroit.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And I would do nothing to hurt the U.S. auto industry.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: My plan to get the industry on its feet when it was in real trouble was not to start writing checks.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It was President Bush that wrote the first checks.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I said they need -- these companies need to go through a managed bankruptcy.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And in that process, they can get government help and government guarantees, but they need to go through bankruptcy to get rid of excess cost and the debt burden that they'd -- they'd built up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Governor Romney, that's not what you said...

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Governor Romney, you did not...

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You did not say that you would provide government help.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I said that we would provide guarantees, and -- and that was what was able to allow these companies to go through bankruptcy, to come out of bankruptcy.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Under no circumstances would I do anything other than to help this industry get on its feet.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And the idea that has been suggested that I would liquidate the industry, of course not.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: That's the height of silliness...

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let -- let -- let's...

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I have never said I would liquidate...

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: ...I would liquidate the industry.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Governor, the people in Detroit don't forget.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: ...and -- and that's why I have the kind of commitment to ensure that our industries in this country can compete and be successful.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We in this country can -- can compete successfully with anyone in the world, and we're going to.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We're going to have to have a president, however, that doesn't think that somehow the government investing in -- in car companies like Tesla and -- and Fisker, making electric battery cars.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: This is not research, Mr President, these are the government investing in companies.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: This is a company, this isn't basic research.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I -- I want to invest in research.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Providing funding to universities and think tanks is great.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The fact of the matter is...

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: So I want to make sure that we make -- we make America more competitive.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And that we do those things that make America the most attractive place in the world for entrepreneurs, innovators, businesses to grow.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But you're investing in companies doesn't do that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: In fact it makes it less likely for them to come here...

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: ...because the private sector's not going to invest in a...

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm -- I'm -- I'm happy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: ...you've had the floor for a while.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The -- look, I think anybody out there can check the record.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Governor Romney, you keep on trying to, you know airbrush history here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You were very clear that you would not provide, government assistance to the U.S. auto companies, even if they went through bankruptcy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You said that they could get it in the private marketplace.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They would have gone through a...

speaker: Barack Obama
text: ...they would have gone through a...

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No, I am not wrong.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: People can look it up, you're right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: People will look it up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But more importantly it is true that in order for us to be competitive, we're going to have to make some smart choices right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Cutting our education budget, that's not a smart choice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Cutting our investments in research and technology, that's not a smart choice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Bringing down our deficit by adding $7 trillion of tax cuts and military spending that our military is not asking for, before we even get to the debt that we currently have, that is not going to make us more competitive.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those are the kinds of choices that the American people face right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Having a tax code that rewards companies that are shipping jobs overseas instead of companies that are investing here in the United States, that will not make us more competitive.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the one thing that I'm absolutely clear about is that after a decade in which we saw drift, jobs being shipped overseas, nobody championing American workers and American businesses, we've now begun to make some real progress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What we can't do is go back to the same policies that got us into such difficulty in the first place.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we have to move forward and not go back.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I couldn't agree more about going forward, but I certainly don't want to go back to the policies of the last four years.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: The policies of the last four years have seen incomes in America decline every year for middle income families, now down $4,300 during your term.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Twenty-three million Americans still struggling to find a good job.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: When you came to office 32 million people on food stamps.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Today, 47 million people on food stamps.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: When you came to office, just over $10 trillion in debt, now $16 trillion in debt.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: You said by now we'd be at 5.4 percent unemployment.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I've met some of those people.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I've met them in Appleton, Wisconsin.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I met a young woman in -- in Philadelphia who's coming out of -- out of college, can't find work.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I've been -- Ann was with someone just the other day that was just weeping about not being able to get work.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: It's just a tragedy in a nation so prosperous as ours, that the last four years have been so hard.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And that's why it's so critical, that we make America once again the most attractive place in the world to start businesses, to build jobs, to grow the economy.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And that's not going to happen by just hiring teachers.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Look, I love to -- I love teachers, and I'm happy to have states and communities that want to hire teachers do that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: By the way, I don't like to have the federal government start pushing its weight deeper and deeper into our schools.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Let the states and localities do that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: The federal government didn't hire our teachers.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: But I want to get our private sector growing and I know how to do it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, thank you very much, Bob, Governor Romney, and to Lynn University.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You've now heard three debates, months of campaigning and way too many TV commercials.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And now you've got a choice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the last four years we've made real progress digging our way out of policies that gave us two prolonged wars, record deficits and the worst economic crisis since the Great Depression.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And Governor Romney wants to take us back to those policies, a foreign policy that's wrong and reckless, economic policies that won't create jobs, won't reduce our deficit, but will make sure that folks at the very top don't have to play by the same rules that you do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I've got a different vision for America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want to build on our strengths.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I've put forward a plan to make sure that we're bringing manufacturing jobs back to our shores by rewarding companies and small businesses that are investing here, not overseas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want to make sure we've got the best education system in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we're retaining our workers for the jobs of tomorrow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want to control our own energy by developing oil and natural gas but also the energy sources of the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As Commander in Chief, I will maintain the strongest military in the world, keep faith with our troops and go after those who would do us harm.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: but after a decade of war, I think we all recognize we've got to do some nation building here at home, rebuilding our roads, our bridges and especially caring for our Veterans who sacrificed so much for our freedom.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will fight for your families and I will work every single day to make sure that America continues to be the greatest nation on earth.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Bob, Mr. President, folks at Lynn University, good to be with you.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'm excited about our prospects as a nation.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I want to see peace.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I want to see growing peace in this country.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We have an opportunity to have real leadership.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: America's going to have that kind of leadership and continue to promote principles of peace to make a world a safer place and make people in this country more confident that their future is secure.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I also want to make sure that we get this economy going.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: And there are two very different paths the country can take.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: One is a path represented by the president, which at the end of four years would mean we'd have $20 trillion in debt heading towards Greece.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'll get us on track to a balanced budget.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: The president's path will mean continuing declining in take-home pay.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I want to make sure our take-home pay turns around and starts to grow.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I want to make sure take-home pay turns around and starts to grow.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: The president's path means 20 million people out of work struggling for a good job.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'll get people back to work with 12 million new jobs.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'm going to make sure that we get people off of food stamps, not by cutting the program, but by getting them good jobs.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: America's going to come back, and for that to happen, we're going to have to have a president who can work across the aisle.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I learned how to get along on the other side of the aisle.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We've got to do that in Washington.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I know what it takes to get this country back, and will work with good Democrats and good Republicans to do that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: This nation is the hope of the earth.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: We've been blessed by having a nation that's free and prosperous thanks to the contributions of the greatest generation.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: They've held a torch for the world to see -- the torch of freedom and hope and opportunity.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: Now, it's our turn to take that torch.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'm convinced we'll do it.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'd like to be that leader with your support.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'll lead you in an open and honest way, and I ask for your vote.

speaker: Mitt Romney
text: I'd like to be the next president of the United States to support and help this great nation and to make sure that we all together remain America as the hope of the earth.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I'm glad you clarified that.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Mr. Hankins, I don't feel good about it, and I think we ought to have a patient's bill of rights to take the medical decisions away from the HMOs and give them back to the doctors and nurses.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I want to come back and tell you why, but if you will forgive me, I would like to say something right now at the beginning of this debate following on the moment of silence for Mel Carnahan and Randy Carnahan and Chris Sifford.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Tipper and I were good friends with Mel and Randy, and I know that all of us here want to extend our sympathy and condolences to Jean and the family and to the Sifford family.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And I would just like to say that this debate in a way is a living tribute to Mel Carnahan because he loved the vigorous discussion of ideas in our democracy.

speaker: Al Gore
text: He was a fantastic governor of Missouri.

speaker: Al Gore
text: This state became one of the top five in the nation for health care coverage for children under his leadership.

speaker: Al Gore
text: One of the best in advancing all kinds of benefits for children to grow up healthy and strong.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And of course, this debate also takes place at a time when the tragedy of the USS Cole is on our minds and hearts and insofar as the memorial service is tomorrow, I would like to also extend sympathy to the families of those who have died and those who are still missing, and the injured.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now, Mr. Hankins, I think that the situation that you describe has gotten completely out of hand.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Doctors are giving prescriptions, they're recommending treatments, and then their recommendations are being overruled by HMOs and insurance companies.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I support a strong national patient's bill of rights.

speaker: Al Gore
text: It is actually a disagreement between us, a national law that is pending on this, the Dingle-Norwood bill, a bipartisan bill, is one that I support and that the governor does not.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I, too, want to extend my prayers and blessings, God's blessings on the families whose lives were overturned yes -- tod -- last night.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Actually, Mr. Vice President, it's not true.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I do support a national patient's bill of rights.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As a matter of fact, I brought Republicans and Democrats together to do just that in the State of Texas to get a patient's bill of rights through.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It requires a different kind of leadership style to do it, though.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You see, in order to get something done on behalf of the people, you have to put partisanship aside, and that's what we did in my state.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have one of the most advanced patient's bill of rights.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It says, for example, that a woman doesn't have to go through a gate keeper to go to her gynecologist.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It says that you can't gag a doctor, doctor can advise you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The HMO, the insurance company, can't gag that doctor from giving you full advice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this particular bill, it allows patients to choose a doctor, their own doctor if they want to.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But we did something else that was interesting.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're one of the first states that said you can sue an HMO for denying you proper coverage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now there's what's called an Independent Review Organization that you have to go through first.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It says if youÃ¢â‚¬â„¢ve got a complaint with your insurance company, you can take your complaint to an objective body.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If the objective body rules on your behalf, the insurance company must follow those rules.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: However, if the insurance company doesn't follow the findings of the IRO, then that becomes a cause of action in a court of law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's time for our nation to come together and do what's right for the people, and I think this is right for the people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You know, I support a national patient's bill of rights, Mr. Vice President, and I want all people covered.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I don't want the law to supersede good law like we've got in Texas.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Jim, we have a direct disagreement on this.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I referred to the Dingle-Norwood bill.

speaker: Al Gore
text: It is the bipartisan bill that is now pending in the Congress.

speaker: Al Gore
text: The HMOs and the insurance companies support the other bill that's pending, the one that the Republican majority has put forward.

speaker: Al Gore
text: They like it because it doesn't accomplish what I think really needs to be accomplished to give the decisions back to the doctors and nurses and give you a right of appeal to somebody other than the HMO or insurance company, let you go to the nearest emergency room without having to call an HMO before you call 911, to let you see a specialist if you need to, and it has strong bipartisan support.

speaker: Al Gore
text: It is being blocked by the Republican leadership in the Congress.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And I specifically would like to know whether Governor Bush will support the Dingle-Norwood bill, which is the main one pending.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Well, the difference is is that I can get it done.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That I can get something positive done on behalf of the people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That's what the question in this campaign is about.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's not only what's your philosophy and what's your position on issues, but can you get things done?

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I believe I can.

speaker: Al Gore
text: What about the Dingle-Norwood bill?

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I talked about the principles and the issues that I think are important in a patient's bill of rights.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's kind of Washington, D.C. focus.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Well, it's in this committee or it's got this sponsor.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If I'm the president, we're going to have emergency room care, we're going have gag orders, we're going to have direct access to OB/GYN.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: People will be able to take their HMO insurance company to court.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That's what I've done in Texas and that's the kind of leadership style I'll bring to Washington.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Well, that's a great question.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I think one of the problems we have, particularly for seniors, is there is no prescription drug coverage in Medicare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And therefore, when they have to try to purchase drugs they do so on their own, there's no kind of collective bargaining, no power of purchasing among seniors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I think step one to make sure prescription drugs is more affordable for seniors, and those are the folks who really rely upon prescription drugs a lot these days, is to reform the Medicare system, is to have prescription drugs as an integral part of Medicare once and for all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The problem we have today is like the patient's bill of rights, particularly with health care, there's a lot of bickering in Washington, D.C.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's kind of like a political issue as opposed to a people issue.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So what I want to do is I want to call upon Republicans and Democrats to forget all the arguing and finger pointing, and come together and take care of our seniors' prescription drug program, that says we'll pay for the poor seniors, we'll help all seniors with prescription drugs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the meantime, I think it's important to have what's called Immediate Helping Hand, which is direct money to states so that seniors, poor seniors, don't have to choose between food and medicine.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That's part of an overall overhaul.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I'm against price controls.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I think price controls would hurt our ability to continue important research and development.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Drug therapies are replacing a lot of medicines as we used to know it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One of the most important things is to continue the research and development component.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so I'm against price controls.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Expediting drugs through the FDA makes sense, of course.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Allowing the new bill that was passed in the Congress made sense to allow for, you know, drugs that were sold overseas to come back and other countries to come back into the United States.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But the best thing to do is to reform Medicare.

speaker: Al Gore
text: All right, here we go again.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now look, if you want someone who will spend a lot of words describing a whole convoluted process and then end up supporting legislation that is supported by the big drug companies, this is your man.

speaker: Al Gore
text: If you want someone who will fight for you and who will fight for the middle-class families and working men and women, who are sick and tired of having their parents and grandparents pay higher prices for prescription drugs than anybody else, then I want to fight for you.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And you asked a great question because it's not only seniors.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Listen, for 24 years I have never been afraid to take on the big drug companies.

speaker: Al Gore
text: They do some great things.

speaker: Al Gore
text: They discover great new cures and that's great.

speaker: Al Gore
text: We want them to continue that.

speaker: Al Gore
text: But they are now spending more money on advertising and promotion.

speaker: Al Gore
text: You see all these ads?

speaker: Al Gore
text: Than they are on research and development.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And they are trying artificially extend the monopoly patent protection so they can keep charging these very high prices.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I want to streamline the approval of the competing generic drugs and the new kinds of treatments that can compete with them so we bring the price down for everybody.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now, briefly, let me tell you how my prescription drug plan works.

speaker: Al Gore
text: The governor talked about Medicare.

speaker: Al Gore
text: You pick your own doctor, and nobody can take that away from you.

speaker: Al Gore
text: The doctor chooses the prescription that you need and nobody can overrule your doctor.

speaker: Al Gore
text: You go to your own pharmacy and then Medicare pays half the price.

speaker: Al Gore
text: If you're poor, they pay all of it.

speaker: Al Gore
text: If you have extraordinarily high cost, then they pay all over $4,000 out-of-pocket.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And I'll bring new competition to bring the price down.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And if you pass the big drug companies' bill, nothing will happen.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I think that we should move step-by-step toward universal health coverage, but I am not in favor of government doing it all.

speaker: Al Gore
text: We've spent 65 years now on the development of a hybrid system, partly private, partly public, and 85% of our people have health insurance, 15% don't.

speaker: Al Gore
text: That adds up to 44 million people.

speaker: Al Gore
text: That is a national outrage.

speaker: Al Gore
text: We have got to get health coverage for those who do not have it and we've got to improve the quality for those who do with a patient's bill of rights that's real and that works, the Dingle-Norwood bill, and we have got to fill in the gaps in coverage by finally bringing parity for the treatment of mental illness, because that's been left out.

speaker: Al Gore
text: We have got to deal with long-term care.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now, here are the steps that I would take, first of all.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I will make a commitment to bring health care coverage of high quality that is affordable to every single child in America within four years.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And then we'll fill other gaps by covering the parents of those children when the family is poor or up to two and a half times the poverty rate.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I want to give a tax credit for the purchase of individual health insurance plans.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I want to give small business employers a tax credit, 25%, to encourage the providing of health insurance for the employees in small businesses.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I want to give seniors who are, well, the near elderly, I don't like that term because I am just about in that category, but those 55 to 65 ought to be able to buy into Medicare for premiums that are reasonable and fair and significantly below what they have to get now.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now, we have a big difference on this.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And you need to know the record here.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Under Governor Bush, Texas has sunk to be 50th out of 50 in health care -- in health insurance for their citizens.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Last week he said that they were spending 3.7 billion dollars, or 4.7 billion dollars on this.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I'm absolutely opposed to a national health care plan.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I don't want the federal government making decisions for consumers or for providers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I remember what the administration tried to do in 1993.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They tried to have a national health care plan.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I trust people, I don't trust the federal government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's going to be one of the themes you hear tonight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I don't want the federal government making decisions on behalf of everybody.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There is an issue with the uninsured, there sure is.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we have uninsured people in my state.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Ours is a big state, a fast-growing state.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We share a common border with another nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But we're providing health care for our people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One thing about insurance, that's a Washington term.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The question is, are people getting health care, and we have a strong safety net, and there needs to be a safety net in America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There needs to be more community health clinics where the poor can go get health care.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need a program for the uninsured.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They've been talking about it in Washington, D.C.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The number of uninsured has now gone up for the past seven years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need a $2,000 credit, rebate for people, working people that don't have insurance, they can get in the marketplace and start purchasing insurance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need to have -- allow small businesses to write insurance across jurisdictional lines so small business can afford health care, small restaurants can afford health care.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So health care needs to be affordable and available.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have to trust people to make decisions with their lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the Medicare reform I talk about it says if you are a senior, you can stay in Medicare if you like it, and that's fine, but we're going to give you other choices to choose if you want to do so, just like they do the federal employees.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The people that work in Washington, D.C. for the U.S. Congress or the United States senate.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Get a variety of choices to make in their lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And that's what we ought to do for all people in America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Trying to find my light.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Well, you know, it's hard to make people love one another.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I wish I knew the law because I would darn sure sign it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I wish I knew the law that said all of us would be good parents.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One of the things the next president must do is to remind people that if we are going to have a responsible period in America, that each of us must love our children with all our heart and all our soul.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I happened to believe strong accountability encourages parental involvement, though.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I think when you measure and post results on the Internet or in the town newspapers, most parents say wait a minute, my child's school isn't doing what I want it to do and, therefore, become involved in education.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I recognize there are some who just don't seem to care.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But there are a lot of parents who feel like everything is going well in their child's school, and all of a sudden they wake up and realize that wait a minute, standards aren't being met.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That's why I'm so strong for accountability.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I believe we ought to measure a lot, three, four, five, six, seven, eighth grade.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We do so in my state of Texas.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One of the good things we've gone in Texas is we have strong accountability because you can't cure unless you know.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You can't solve a problem unless you diagnose it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I strongly believe that one of the best things to encourage parental involvement also is to know that the classrooms will be safe and secure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That's why I support a teacher liability act at the federal level, that says if a teacher or principal upholds reasonable standards of classroom discipline they can't be sued.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I think parents will be more involved with education when they know their children's classrooms are safe and secure as well.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I also believe that we need to say to people that if you cannot meet standards, there has to be a consequence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Instead of just comes the soft bigotry of low expectations, that there has to be a consequence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can't continue to shuffle children through school.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And one of the consequences to allow parents to have different choices.

speaker: Al Gore
text: We have huge difference between us on this question.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I'd like to start by telling you what my vision is.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I see a day in the United States of America where all of our public schools are considered excellent, world class.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Where there are no failing schools, where the classrooms are small enough in size, number of students, so that the teacher can spend enough one-on-one time with each student.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now that means recruiting new teachers for the public schools.

speaker: Al Gore
text: It means in my plan hiring bonuses to get 100,000 new teachers in the public schools within the next four years.

speaker: Al Gore
text: It means also helping local school districts that sometimes find the parents of school age children outvoted on bond issues, to give them some help with interest-free bonding authority so that we can build new schools and modernize the classrooms.

speaker: Al Gore
text: We need to give teachers the training and professional development that they need, including a paid time off to go visit the classroom of a master teacher to pick up some new skills.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I want to give every middle-class family a $10,000 a year tax deduction for college tuition so that middle-class families will always be able to send their kids on to college.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I want to work for universal free school because we know from all the studies that the youngsters learn, kids learn more in the first few years of life than any where else.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now, I said there was a contrast.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Governor Bush is for vouchers, and in his plan he proposes to drain more money, more taxpayer money out of the public schools for private school vouchers than all of the money that he proposes in his entire budget for public schools themselves.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And only one in 20 students would be eligible for these vouchers, and they wouldn't even pay the full tuition to private school.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I don't think we should give up on the private schools and leave kids trapped in failing schools.

speaker: Al Gore
text: I think we -- I think we should make it the number one priority to make our schools the best in the world, all of them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I think any time we end with one of these attacks, it's appropriate to respond.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: First of all, vouchers are up to states.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I strongly believe in local control of schools.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I'm a governor of state and I don't like it when the federal government tells us what to do.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I believe in local control of schools.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But here's what I said.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I've said to the extent we spend federal money on disadvantaged children, we want the schools to show us whether or not the children are learning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We expect there to be standards met and we expect there to be measurement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And if we find success we'll praise it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But when we find children trapped in schools that will not change and will not teach, instead of saying oh, this is okay in America just to shuffle poor kids through schools, there has to be a consequence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the consequence is that federal portion or federal money will go to the parent, so the parent can go to a tutoring program or another public school or another private school.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You see, there has to be a consequence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've got a society that says hey, the status quo is fine, just move them through.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Well, the program that he's proposing is not the one that he just described.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Described under your plan, Governor Bush, states would be required to pay vouchers to students to match the vouchers so that the federal government would put up.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now, you're -- and the way it would happen is that under his plan, if a school was designated as failing, the kids would be trapped there for another three years and then some of them would get federal vouchers and the state would be forced to match those, that money.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Under my plan, if a school is failing, we work with the states to give them the authority and the resources to close down that school and reopen it right away with a new principal, a new faculty, a turn-around team of specialists who know what they're doing.

speaker: Al Gore
text: It's based on the plan of Governor Jim Hunt in North Carolina, and it works great.

speaker: Al Gore
text: If I thought that there was no alternative, then I might feel differently.

speaker: Al Gore
text: But I have an obligation to fight to make sure there are no failing schools.

speaker: Al Gore
text: We have to turn around -- most schools are excellent, but we have to make sure that all of them are.

speaker: Al Gore
text: What grade do you teach?

speaker: Al Gore
text: I mentioned before that the local communities are having a harder time passing bond issues.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Traditionally, if you've been involved in a campaign like that, you know that the parents with kids in school are the ones that turn out and vote.

speaker: Al Gore
text: It's ironic that there are now -- there is now a smaller percentage of the voters made up of parents with children than ever in American history because of the aging of our population, but at the same time we've got the largest generation of students in public schools ever.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And it's the largest number ever this year and they'll break the record next year and every year for ten years running.

speaker: Al Gore
text: We've got to do something about this.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And local -- it's not enough to leave it up to the local school districts.

speaker: Al Gore
text: They're not able to do it and our future depends upon it.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Look, we're in an information age.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Our economic future depends upon whether or not our children are going to get the kind of education that lets them go on to college.

speaker: Al Gore
text: And again, I want to make it possible for all middle-class families to send their kids to college and more Pell grants for those who are in the lower income groups also, and then I want to make sure that we have job training on top of that and lifelong learning, but it all starts with the public school teachers.

speaker: Al Gore
text: My proposal gives $10,000 hiring bonuses for those teachers who are -- who get certified to teach in the areas where they're most needed.

speaker: Al Gore
text: Now, accountability, we basically agree on accountability.

speaker: Al Gore
text: My plan requires testing of all students.

speaker: Al Gore
